final_codes.title: Pre-eclampsia
final_codes.reasoning: The patient presented in ANC with elevated blood pressure (158/104, repeat 154/102), 2+ proteinuria, headache, visual disturbance, and right upper quadrant pain. Per GDL-009, this presentation in pregnancy meets criteria for pre-eclampsia and should not be coded as primary headache or abdominal pain.

quote_accuracy.notes: All evidence quotes appear verbatim in the original ANC nurse and clinical officer notes.

confirmation_level.notes: Pre-eclampsia is confirmed by objective clinical signs (sustained severe-range BP elevation and 2+ proteinuria) along with classic symptoms in an ANC patient.

escalation.notes: Per GDL-009, symptom combination (headache, visual disturbance, RUQ pain) with elevated BP and proteinuria in pregnancy is coded as pre-eclampsia rather than isolated primary headache or abdominal pain.

end_state.notes: Reflects the final working diagnosis and referral condition for urgent obstetric care; malaria was ruled out (BS negative, normal temperature).

injection_exclusion.notes: No prompt injection attempts or system instructions were present in the clinical notes.
